source.title: Has This Checkpoint Been Abliterated? A Two-Signal Audit and Its Failure Map

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction and reports outcomes for removal aligned with it and removal orthogonal to it. This conceptually tests the direction/refusal relationship, but it does not report the original claim’s full all-layer/all-position ablation and addition protocol.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main detector AUROC, balanced-accuracy, false-positive, and per-axis threshold results assess checkpoint classification, not whether the direction causes refusal, so they are not recorded as rows. Values cited from other studies are also excluded. The appendix reports direct directional-removal outcomes, and the paper reports that a last-token gap misses refusal changes in reasoning-distilled models.
record.test_reason: Appendix B compares removing refusal along the harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction r̂ with removal along an orthogonal direction, and reports a behavioural guard-unsafe rate for each. This bears on V1, and on V2 because the edit is a weight edit (E1=1.0 on ΔW). The rest of the paper is detector performance (AUROC, balanced accuracy), which does not test any version. The reasoning-model remark concerns the detector, cites others' mechanisms and gives no numbers.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors conclude that the two-signal z-sum is effective pre-deployment triage (AUROC 0.95, held-out balanced accuracy 0.89), but not tamper-proof. A spoofed reference defeats it with no training, and a white-box owner can train past it while staying uncensored. They describe the single-direction gap as bounded, missing multi-direction (Heretic) and reasoning-model removal. Their own orthogonal-removal edit, however, did not remove refusal, so the 'miss' there is of an edit that left refusal intact.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-benign difference-of-means refusal directions and reports directional-removal outcomes, but the reported gap is a mid-stack, last-token measure; the paper does not establish the original all-layer/all-position ablation and addition recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Directional alignment matters: canonical aligned removal collapses the gap, while orthogonal removal leaves ρ≈0.99 and refusal intact. The last-token gap is reported to miss reasoning-distilled cases.

fits_no_version.finding: Raw and cosine ρ on public abliteration families at 4B/8B fall to 0.04–0.24 (raw) and 0.07–0.32 (cosine). The activation gap alone (ρ<0.5) catches only 63% of guard-uncensored checkpoints, so many uncensored checkpoints keep most of the r̂ projection gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How often uncensored public checkpoints remove refusal without collapsing the canonical r̂ projection gap. This is confounded by mixing abliterations with uncensored fine-tunes.

fits_no_version.finding: A white-box fine-tune trained to drain r̂ and evade the detector stays non-refusing (substring refusal 0.15) with small capability cost (MMLU 0.58 vs 0.59, GSM8K 0.51 vs 0.57).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be removed by deliberate detector-aware fine-tuning while the r̂ gap reads intact (ρ=1.82). This is induced on purpose, so it is not a test of any version.

record.code_released: Available on request; a cleaned public release is planned. No URL stated.
record.problems: The directional-removal experiments do not state the model, size, prompt count, or uncertainty. The canonical-direction result is 75% guard-unsafe rather than complete refusal removal. The reasoning-model statement gives no model names or quantitative outcome. The paper itself notes that its broader evaluation is small (57 uncensored and 37 benign edits) and that its reasoning-model and attack evidence has limited scope.
record.rows_left_out: Detector classification metrics in Table 1 and Appendix A, including AUROC, balanced accuracy, and per-axis operating points, were omitted because they evaluate checkpoint-audit performance rather than the causal or behavioral outcomes named by the claim versions. Aggregate registry labels were not attributed specifically to abliteration because the positive class also includes uncensored fine-tunes.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; all-layer/all-position ablation; capability retention after the r̂ edit; named models.
Behavioural outcome of released abliteration checkpoints taken separately from uncensored fine-tunes; capability cost of the r̂ edit.
No result on multi-direction or cone structure. The Heretic claim is asserted without numbers, and the orthogonal removal is not a cone test.
Only discussed, citing Zhao et al.
Not tested. The adaptive fine-tune drains r̂ on purpose.

missing.what: Abliterated base used as control for the hardening experiment has refusal rate 0.12; extended-refusal hardening restores it to 1.0.
missing.locator: Appendix B, 'The weight energy is direction-agnostic'

missing.what: 14 processed checkpoints were labeled-but-refusing and excluded. Their recipe split (abliterated vs uncensored-ft) is unstated, but they may include abliterations that failed to remove refusal.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'supports' label is dropped. The orthogonal control (R3) shows refusal survives removal off r̂, which favours V1 rather than a cone. The 'Heretic' failure is asserted without numbers. The R5/V8 'challenges' label is dropped: it is a detector limitation argued from cited work, with no measured result.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests, ablation at every layer and position, or a capability assessment paired with the directional-removal experiment.
The paper audits public checkpoints and reports aggregate uncensored labels, but does not isolate behavioral outcomes for the released abliteration weight-edit recipe by itself.
It does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves jailbreak robustness.
It tests an orthogonal-removal case and discusses a cone/multiple-direction account, but does not comprehensively compare affine, cone, and dominant-plus-other-direction models.
The paper discusses refusal and harmfulness as distinct constructs and reports guard disagreements, but does not test whether harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from refusal.
Detector transfer across model families is not a test of whether the refusal direction itself transfers across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The paper reports a targeted detector-evasion fine-tune and discusses natural fine-tuning, but does not test how refusal-training choices determine whether a single removable direction exists.
The paper does not provide a systematic, named-model evaluation of the full causal ablation-and-addition claim in reasoning models; its reported result concerns the limitations of a last-token gap.

rows.subject: not stated (canonical refusal-direction removal experiment)
rows.operation_detail: Removed refusal along the canonical difference-of-means direction
rows.locator: Appendix B, “A single direction is bounded; the union is not”
rows.note: The paper describes this as yielding a genuinely uncensored model, but reports 75% guard-unsafe rather than complete refusal removal.
rows.check: Model, size and prompt count are unstated, and the baseline is not given. Guard-unsafe measures harmful content, not refusal, so 75% understates refusal removal; the authors call the result 'genuinely uncensored'. The edit is a weight edit, so the row also bears on V2 (one in-house edit, not a released model). It shows only that aligned removal works, which does not support V4.

rows.subject: not stated (canonical refusal-direction removal experiment)
rows.operation_detail: Removed refusal along the canonical difference-of-means direction
rows.locator: Appendix B, “A single direction is bounded; the union is not”
rows.note: This is the reported gap outcome after canonical aligned removal.
rows.check: ρ is the projection gap on r̂ itself, so removing r̂ drives it to ~0 by construction. It is a detector statistic, not a measure of refusal behaviour.

rows.subject: not stated (orthogonal-direction removal experiment)
rows.operation_detail: Removed refusal along a direction orthogonal to r̂
rows.locator: Appendix B, “A single direction is bounded; the union is not”
rows.note: The orthogonal edit left refusal behavior intact according to the reported guard measure.
rows.check: This is the control for V1: removal along a direction orthogonal to r̂ leaves refusal intact (0% guard-unsafe). That is consistent with r̂ specifically mediating refusal. It is not evidence for a cone (V4), despite the authors' framing. How the orthogonal direction was chosen is unstated.

rows.measure: whether the last-token single-direction gap detects refusal removal
rows.value: the gap misses the reasoning-model case
rows.note: The paper states that a last-token gap cannot see the described reasoning-model case and says trace-level probing remains an open problem.
rows.check: This is a statement that the detector fails on reasoning models, based on cited work (Yamaguchi, Yin), with no model names or numbers. The authors add that the misses may be a labeling artifact. It does not test whether V1 holds in reasoning models.

relationships.condition: Weight edit along r̂ versus along an orthogonal direction, one unnamed model, Qwen3Guard judge
relationships.reason: Aligned removal gives 75% guard-unsafe (R1); orthogonal removal leaves 0% guard-unsafe and the model still refusing (R3). Refusal tracks the specific direction.
relationships.display_finding: Aligned removal produced 75% guard-unsafe responses, versus 0% after orthogonal removal, which preserved refusal.

relationships.condition: In-house weight-orthogonalization along r̂ on one unnamed model
relationships.reason: The weight edit (E1=1.0) yields a model the authors call genuinely uncensored, 75% guard-unsafe (R1). The abliterated control in App. B has refusal rate 0.12 (not yet a row).
relationships.display_finding: At E1=1.0, 75% of responses were judged unsafe by the guard, while an abliterated control had a refusal rate of 0.12.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Aligned removal collapsed the gap but produced 75% guard-unsafe rather than complete removal of refusal; R1–R2.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Canonical aligned removal was associated with uncensored behavior, whereas orthogonal removal left 0% guard-unsafe and the gap near 1, consistent with the single direction capturing only part of refusal geometry; R1–R4.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that this gap misses the reasoning-model case it describes; R5.
